title: Production Incident: Cloud Provider IAM & Stripe Key Leak in CI Logs
businessContext: A public GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow log for an open-source client SDK printed the entire environment configuration, exposing production AWS Access Keys (`AKIA...`) and live Stripe API Secret Keys (`sk_live_...`).
problemStatement: Triage this active security emergency. Identify the immediate containment actions (revocation, key rotation, active session invalidation), audit access logs for unauthorized access/exfiltration, fix the pipeline to prevent secret echo, and author a blameless post-mortem with preventative guardrails (git-secrets, AWS KMS, IAM least privilege).
constraints: Treat the leaked credentials as compromised immediately.
Must rotate keys without causing prolonged production downtime.
Audit CloudTrail and Stripe Dashboard audit logs for unauthorized anomalous activity.

logs.message: Workflow run #842 started on branch main (public repo)

recentDeployments.author: dev-intern
recentDeployments.message: ci: print env variables to debug build failure

candidateTasks: Step 1: Immediate Revocation - List exact steps to revoke leaked IAM credentials and Stripe secret key.
Step 2: Threat Assessment - Identify what AWS CloudTrail APIs were called (e.g. ec2:RunInstances for cryptomining) and terminate unauthorized resources.
Step 3: Invalidate Active Sessions - Force-revoke temporary STS tokens and rotate Stripe webhook signing secret.
Step 4: Pipeline Remediation - Remove `printenv`, enable secret masking, and switch to OIDC (OpenID Connect) for short-lived credentials instead of static IAM keys.
Step 5: Write Root Cause Analysis & Prevention Plan.
hints: Never wait to see if keys are abused: assume automated bot scraping finds leaked keys within 30 seconds of commit.
Replace static long-lived AWS IAM access keys with GitHub Actions OIDC role assumption.
alternativeApproaches: Using AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault with dynamic secret engines for automated credential rotation.
commonMistakes: Deleting the GitHub log or making the repo private without rotating the keys (scrapers index keys within seconds).
Creating a new key without deactivating the old compromised key.
